passage: I am Irawati, and I want to talk about the worst week of my second year. The lab report was due on Friday, my last reading was wrong, and I copied a result from a classmate's sheet to finish on time. I handed it in, and that night I could not sleep. My chest felt tight, and I kept thinking, what if someone checks? Two nights later I went to Asif sir and said, "I copied a value in my report. I'd like to redo the experiment." My hands were cold. He was quiet, then said, "Thank you for telling me now." I redid it over the weekend. I lost some marks, but I also saw that my whole plan had been too tight. Now I start early and ask for help sooner.

qa.q: On which day was the lab report due?
qa.a: The report was due on Friday.

qa.q: Why could Irawati not sleep after handing in the report?
qa.a: Irawati felt guilty and worried that someone would check, so the guilt and fear kept Irawati awake with a tight chest.

qa.q: What could Irawati do the next time a deadline feels impossible?
qa.a: Irawati can start earlier, ask for help sooner, and speak to the supervisor before copying anything.

qa.q: How might Asif sir have seen Irawati's admission?
qa.a: He was quiet, then thanked Irawati for telling him now, so he probably valued the honesty and could still take it seriously. The passage does not say what else he thought.

grounding: The protagonist copied a result to meet a deadline and cannot sleep, then corrects it and admits it early to the right person.

passage: At 2 a.m. in the girls' hostel of the Chennai engineering college, Lavanya was still awake. That afternoon, racing the lab report deadline, she had copied the last two readings from her lab partner's sheet because her own trial had failed. The report was submitted. No one would check. But her stomach wouldn't stop turning. At 9 a.m. she was outside the lab, waiting for Divyansh, the PhD student who ran their section. Her hands were cold. 'I need to correct something in my report,' she said. 'The last two readings aren't mine. My trial failed and I panicked about the deadline.' Divyansh was quiet for a moment. 'Thank you for telling me before I graded it. Redo the trial on Thursday, and write what happened in the notes.' She nodded. Walking out, she felt lighter than she had in hours, and wrote a new rule in her planner: start lab reports on the day of the lab, not the night before.

qa.q: How many readings did Lavanya copy?
qa.a: Lavanya copied the last two readings.

qa.q: What was Lavanya feeling at 2 a.m.?
qa.a: Lavanya felt guilty and uneasy, her stomach turning even though nobody would check.

qa.q: What made Lavanya's next steps wise?
qa.a: She admitted it early to Divyansh before grading, agreed to redo the trial, and changed her habits to avoid deadline panic.

qa.q: How does Divyansh respond to Lavanya's admission?
qa.a: Divyansh thanks her for telling before grading and gives a fair way to fix it.

grounding: Shows a student who copied readings under deadline pressure and can't sleep, then admitting it early, correcting it and learning from the pressure.

passage:
Subject: Correction to the Q2 inventory report
Dear Pradeep-sir,
I need to correct something in the report I sent you yesterday, before it goes to the regional office.
The stock count for the Hadapsar warehouse is not a fresh count. On Tuesday I ran out of time, and I copied last month's figure instead of waiting for the new one. I told myself it would be close enough. I haven't slept well since, and I don't want a number I know is wrong to go further with my name on it.
I called the warehouse this morning. The real count will reach me by 3 p.m. today, and I'll send you the corrected report by 4.
I'm sorry. I think the pressure of finishing four reports on the same day pushed me into a shortcut. Could we talk about spacing the deadlines next month?
Regards,
Sarita

qa.q: Which warehouse's stock count was copied?
qa.a: The Hadapsar warehouse's stock count was copied.

qa.q: What has Sarita been feeling since sending the report?
qa.a: Sarita has felt guilty and restless, not sleeping well because of the wrong number.

qa.q: Why is Sarita's email a wise way to fix it?
qa.a: It admits the problem early to the right person, gives a concrete correction by 4 p.m., and raises the deadline pressure that caused it.

qa.q: What would change for Pradeep-sir if Sarita had buried it?
qa.a: Pradeep-sir might have sent a wrong figure to the regional office and later lost trust in all of Sarita's reports.

grounding: An email shows Sarita admitting a copied figure early to the right person, correcting it, and naming the deadline pressure behind it.
